official_sources: HMLR Practice Guide 62A rights to light or air
HMLR Practice Guide 79 local land charges
official_measurement_examples: a right to natural light through a defined aperture can be an easement
rights to light can arise through more than one legal route
HMLR may require local-land-charge evidence when registering specified prescriptive rights
light obstruction notices have a distinct statutory function
planning daylight/sunlight assessment is not the same as a private right to light
planning permission does not automatically extinguish a right to light
absence of a simple register entry does not by itself prove no right exists
rights-to-light evidence does not establish ownership access capacity or final development yield
core_rules: right to light is not planning policy
planning permission does not extinguish private right automatically
planning daylight assessment is not legal easement test
easement and restrictive covenant remain distinct
light obstruction notice is distinct from planning notice
register entry may not be complete legal history
local land charge search is not title ownership proof
right to light does not establish land ownership
right to light does not establish access rights
right to light does not prove building compliance
right to light does not calculate development yield
no parcel rights-to-light clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
